newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma expected to remove Ukrainian premier.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma expected to remove Ukrainian premier.

text.p: An aide to Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Tuesday that President Leonid Kuchma was likely to confirm his removal from office this week.
Lazarenko was taken to a government hospital last month and replaced "for the time of his illness" by his deputy Vasyl Durdynets, but there were varying accounts of what was wrong with him.
Interfax-Ukraine news agency said a presidential decree would probably be issued on Tuesday saying Lazarenko had been removed at his own request.
Asked to comment, the Lazarenko aide said: "I am not sure it will happen on Tuesday, but it could happen on Wednesday or more likely by the end of the week."
A spokeswoman for Kuchma's office said there was "no decree yet" on Lazarenko's position.
Lazarenko's delivery to hospital on June 19 was widely seen as a ploy and a sign that Kuchma planned to remove him from power.
The chief doctor at the hospital outside Kiev where Lazarenko is being treated said he had a form of acute varicose veins which can eventually lead to a stroke or heart attack.

For months Kuchma has been under pressure from Western and Ukrainian officials to dismiss Lazarenko, who has been blamed for a poor record on economic reforms and accused of being too close to the lucrative energy sector.
